🧭 Local travel essentials
Getting around
Subway (Lines 1–9, Sinbundang Line, etc.) and city buses dominate the Capital Region. Integrated multi-modal transit system. Standard transit cards: T-money and Cashbee—accepted at nearly all transit and convenience stores.
See more
Late-night transit
Last subway trains depart around midnight–12:30 AM (varies by line; outbound routes run later). N Bus (Owl Bus) operates major late-night routes. Taxis and Kakao T ride-hailing widely available with late-night surcharge.
Payment
Cards and mobile payments (Samsung Pay, etc.) widely accepted. Street vendors and small transactions may need cash. QR codes (Kakao Pay, Naver Pay) are common.
Currency & exchange
Currency: Korean won (KRW, ₩). Card payments are standard, so exchange needs are minimal. ATMs and exchange bureaus available at airports and city centers.
Language
Korean is the main language. Major tourist sites, concert venues, and transit have English signage. Day-to-day English varies—moderate overall.
Local apps
Kakao T (Taxis, driver services, and ride-hailing available) · Naver Map (Public transit routes & real-time directions) · Kakao Pay (QR codes, quick-pay)
Late-night transit
Kakao T (Night-taxi standard (90%+ market share, fastest matching). Foreign phone sign-up restricted.) · Uber (Taxi hailing—bring your overseas card & number. Made for travelers.) · TADA (Carnival vans—sign up with your overseas number & card.) · i.M (Book premium minivan taxis.) · K-RIDE (Traveler-only taxis (no KakaoTalk; Seoul, Incheon & metro).) · Owl Bus (Seoul Night Bus) (After last train: night buses—official Seoul routes (N15, N16, N26 & more).)  📶 eSIM ↗
How to book
Don't hail from the venue—walk 1–2 blocks out, you'll match faster. Go a station farther, demand drops.
Around the venue
Olive Young Sindorim Branch 📍Major Olive Young nearest Gocheok Sky Dome. One-stop K-beauty shopping.
Hongdae Street 📍Busking, indie music, street fashion—where K-culture thrives. A must-see for international fans.
